Avogadro guide · Minecraft 1.12.2 / Cleanroom

Two fictional atom examples

An optional appendix for authored game elements. These examples illustrate the display API, not predictions of real chemistry or nuclear stability.

Example language Your choice applies across the guides.
Imports and complete companion files

Examples are methods inside the downloadable companion classes. Copy the methods you need into your own class and keep the imports at the top. GuideModels contains the reusable chemical recipes; GuideTasks contains the operations. These files are documentation examples, not built-in library content.

Java model recipes · Java operations · Complete Groovy model script · Groovy client helpers

The complete Groovy model script can be saved as groovy/postInit/avogadro_examples.groovy. It includes the reusable GuideModels class and registers all ten chemical examples through the reloadable script registry. The separate client helper download is a reference for client integrations: keep it out of common postInit scripts and dedicated-server entry points. Java users should likewise copy common operations into their common class and keep screen/export operations in a client class.

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.*;

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.molecule.*;

// Client code only:

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.client.*;

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.client.export.*;

import java.util.List;

import java.util.Map;

Naquadah: an invented neutral atom

Java · method inside your host class; imports and full files below.

public static MoleculeSpec fictionalNaquadah() {

    // Fictional nucleus and chosen shell layout, not a prediction of a real element.

    return AvogadroApi.builder("guide:naquadah").name("Naquadah (fictional)")

            .atom("Nq", 0, 0, 0).noBonds()

            .element("Nq", 174, 352, 2, 8, 18, 32, 50, 32, 18, 14).build();

}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described.

static MoleculeSpec fictionalNaquadah() {

    // Fictional nucleus and chosen shell layout, not a prediction of a real element.

    return AvogadroApi.builder("guide:naquadah").name("Naquadah (fictional)")

            .atom("Nq", 0, 0, 0).noBonds()

            .element("Nq", 174, 352, 2, 8, 18, 32, 50, 32, 18, 14).build();

}

JSON · one definition per file unless a different destination is shown.

{

  "name": "Naquadah (fictional)",

  "atoms": [

    {

      "e": "Nq",

      "x": 0,

      "y": 0,

      "z": 0

    }

  ],

  "bonds": [],

  "elements": {

    "Nq": {

      "atomic_number": 174,

      "neutrons": 352,

      "electron_shells": [

        2,

        8,

        18,

        32,

        50,

        32,

        18,

        14

      ]

    }

  }

}

The chosen shell counts sum to 174 and satisfy the API’s count limits. That validates the data format, not whether such an atom could exist. There is no standard atomic weight for Nq; do not advertise a standard-weight molecular mass.

The same fictional nucleus with every electron removed

Java · method inside your host class; imports and full files below.

public static MoleculeSpec fictionalStrippedIon() {

    // Same fictional nucleus with no electrons: an illustration of explicit ion data.

    return AvogadroApi.builder("guide:naquadah_nucleus").name("Bare naquadah nucleus (fictional)")

            .atom("Nq", 0, 0, 0).noBonds().atomConfiguration(0, 174, 352, 174).build();

}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described.

static MoleculeSpec fictionalStrippedIon() {

    // Same fictional nucleus with no electrons: an illustration of explicit ion data.

    return AvogadroApi.builder("guide:naquadah_nucleus").name("Bare naquadah nucleus (fictional)")

            .atom("Nq", 0, 0, 0).noBonds().atomConfiguration(0, 174, 352, 174).build();

}

JSON · one definition per file unless a different destination is shown.

{

  "name": "Bare naquadah nucleus (fictional)",

  "atoms": [

    {

      "e": "Nq",

      "x": 0,

      "y": 0,

      "z": 0

    }

  ],

  "bonds": [],

  "atom_configurations": {

    "0": {

      "atomic_number": 174,

      "neutrons": 352,

      "charge": 174,

      "electron_shells": []

    }

  }

}

A charge of +174 and no shell entries explicitly gives zero electrons. This demonstrates a nucleus-only inspection case. Stability, energy, radiation, and material properties are outside this rendering API.
